differences.title: 1. DATA MODEL
differences.leftDesc: TiKV stores data as a sorted map of bytes to bytes, offering flexible schema design and direct access to data by its key.
differences.rightDesc: CockroachDB uses a relational model with tables, rows, and columns, enforcing schema and providing SQL query capabilities for complex data relationships.

differences.title: 2. CONSISTENCY MODEL
differences.leftDesc: Employs Raft for distributed consensus, ensuring strong consistency and transactional integrity across all data replicas for reliable operations.
differences.rightDesc: Leverages its own distributed consensus protocol, ensuring strong consistency and serializability for all transactions across geographically distributed nodes.

differences.title: 3. ARCHITECTURE
differences.leftDesc: TiKV focuses solely on distributed transactional storage, allowing compute layers like TiDB to scale independently for optimized performance.
differences.rightDesc: CockroachDB integrates storage and compute into each node, simplifying deployment but potentially limiting independent scaling of resource-intensive tasks.

differences.title: 4. SCALABILITY
differences.leftDesc: Scales out by adding more TiKV nodes, distributing data and load automatically to handle massive throughput and storage growth.
differences.rightDesc: Scales out by adding more nodes, automatically rebalancing data and query load for seamless growth and high availability.

differences.title: 5. QUERYING
differences.leftDesc: Accessed primarily through its client interfaces, often via gRPC, providing low-level key-value operations and transaction management.
differences.rightDesc: Offers a full-fledged SQL interface, enabling complex joins, aggregations, and ad-hoc queries on structured relational data.

differences.title: 6. USE CASES
differences.leftDesc: Ideal for scenarios requiring massive key-value storage, distributed transactions, and high-performance data access with flexible schemas.
differences.rightDesc: Suited for mission-critical applications needing globally distributed, resilient relational databases with strong consistency and SQL compliance.

differences.title: 7. COMMUNITY & ECOSYSTEM
differences.leftDesc: Part of the TiDB ecosystem, it's an open-source project with active development and a strong focus on distributed database solutions.
differences.rightDesc: A well-established open-source distributed SQL database with a robust community and extensive enterprise adoption and support.
